comment: The 2019 cram-js paper's benchmark, re-run against today's library and today's
samtools. paper-2019/ holds the original harness and its raw results; this file
Two fixture groups, and they answer different questions. 'paper2019' is the
corpus the paper itself used, fetched by ../shell/fetch_paper2019.sh — the only
way to say anything about the published numbers as published. 'corpus' is this
repo's own simulated corpus, which every other benchmark here reads, so the
cram-vs-samtools ratio sits on the same bytes as sweep.md and alignments.md.
Neither substitutes for the other and the report never pools them.
The cram-js arms come from the sweep builds (.libs/cram-js/sweep/<tag>), so
every version in the table was built by one pipeline with one toolchain, and a
difference between arms is library code. v1.7.4 is the last of the 1.x line the
paper ran; v13.4.1 is the current release. Add or remove tags here, or override
'contigs' is how many leading sequences of the reference a random interval may
land in. 24 is chr1-chr22, chrX, chrY, which is what the paper drew from — the
GRCh38 analysis set continues with chrM, the alts and the decoys, and a browser
query on a decoy contig is not a case anyone cares about.
